picks.title: Amazon's Alexa+ AI assistant is now free for anyone with a Fire TV device
picks.excerpt: Amazon dropped the $20/month fee and is giving Alexa+ free to every US Fire TV owner, pushing conversational, context-aware assistance onto the living-room screen at once. The TV becomes the default surface for agentic voice UI, and remote-plus-voice navigation design is suddenly a mass-market problem.
picks.rationale: Removing the paywall makes conversational AI the default TV interface overnight — the biggest same-day shift in where assistant UX has to be designed.

picks.title: Even ICE Thinks Smart Glasses Are a Privacy Liability
picks.excerpt: ICE has banned its employees from wearing smart glasses, warning the devices could "unintentionally capture, record or transmit sensitive information." When even a surveillance agency bans always-on camera eyewear, the social-acceptability problem designers keep waving away becomes a hard product constraint.
picks.rationale: A surveillance agency banning camera eyewear turns wearable social acceptability from a soft debate into a documented deployment constraint.

picks.title: Millions of Comcast WiFi Routers Can Now Tell When You're Moving Around the House
picks.excerpt: Comcast is rolling out Xfinity Shield with WiFi Motion, turning ordinary routers into whole-home presence sensors with no new hardware and no camera. Sensing is quietly migrating into infrastructure people never chose as a sensor, which reframes what ambient-AI interfaces have to disclose.
picks.rationale: Presence sensing arriving via a firmware update to hardware nobody bought as a sensor rewrites the consent and disclosure layer of ambient-AI design.

picks.title: macOS Golden Gate adds a new app to your Mac; here's what it can do
picks.excerpt: macOS 27 introduces a standalone Siri app for the Mac — a first — with persistent conversation history and iCloud sync across devices. The assistant graduates from an invisible overlay to a real window with navigation, history and state that has to be designed like any other app.
picks.rationale: Siri becoming a window with history and state is the moment assistant UX stops being an overlay and starts needing real app-level information architecture.

picks.title: A $200 device replaced my phone's biggest job, and now I record meetings without killing the battery
picks.excerpt: The Comu Action Pro is a $200 dedicated AI recorder with six adaptive mics, a magnetic phone mount and about 70 hours of battery that auto-transfers and transcribes what it captures. It is the strongest argument yet that single-purpose AI hardware beats a phone app when the job is capture-and-transcribe.
picks.rationale: A shipping $200 single-purpose AI device that beats the phone app is the clearest current case for when dedicated AI hardware is the right form factor.
